interest: Documents 1930s convict labor reports and the 1934 Tohoku famine's forced daughter-indenturing amid Japan's rising military spending.
overview: File 894.5048 covers 1930s involuntary labor: a cross-reference to a Tokyo despatch on Japanese convict and compulsory labor under U.S. tariff law, and a 1934 Denver citizen's letter on the Tohoku famine forcing families to indenture daughters into brothels and factories, urging international protest and relief.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a diplomatic report from Tokyo regarding convict and compulsory labor in Japan under U.S. tariff laws.
subfiles.summary: Indexes a March 1930 Tokyo report on Japanese convict and compulsory labor under U.S. tariff provisions.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Japanese Convict and Compulsory Labor

subfiles.about: Letter from a Denver resident urging international diplomatic protest and humanitarian assistance regarding reports of indentured labor in famine-stricken Japan.
subfiles.summary: Dudley O. Paterson of Denver urges a joint international protest and humanitarian aid offer over reported exploitation of distressed Japanese agrarian communities.
subfiles.title: Letter from Dudley O. Paterson Proposing Joint International Protest and Relief for Japan

subfiles.about: Syndicated press dispatch detailing the indenturing of young rural women and girls amid severe famine in northern Japan.
subfiles.summary: News clipping: repeated crop failures in six northern Japanese prefectures drove destitute families to indenture an estimated 60,000 daughters to Yoshiwara brokers, cafes, and factories, even as the Cabinet approved a record military budget.
subfiles.title: Press Clipping on Famine Distress and Indentured Servitude in Northern Japan
